The 9-0 UCLA Bruins will be playing with a chip on their shoulder after being ranked No. 4 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings, one spot below the 7-2 Alabama Crimson Tide. They'll face the Illinois Fighting Illini tonight. The Houston Cougars will hit the road to take on the Colorado Buffaloes. The Cougars are in the mix in the Big 12 and at No. 14 in the latest playoff rankings; they have a legitimate chance to make it to the postseason. Let's dive into my best bets for tonight. Miller OVER 0.5 Goals (+235) Yesterday: 0-4 (-$100) Year-to-date: 546-592-15 (-$258.77) pic.twitter.com/A6yfspzN3y Florida State vs. Pittsburgh Best Bet This ACC game is a showdown between one of the best defenses in the conference and one of the worst. Pittsburgh ranks 30th in the country in opponent-adjusted EPA and 10th in defensive success rate. Meanwhile, Florida State ranks 104th and 102nd in those two metrics. Florida State's best offensive weapon is running the football, but now they have to face a Panthers defense that's fourth in the country in opponent EPA per rush and third in opponent rush success rate. If the Seminoles can't move the ball, it's going to be tough for them to be competitive in a road game against Pittsburgh. I'll lay the points with the home team. Pick: Pittsburgh -3.5 (-108) Illinois vs. UCLA Best Bet UCLA somehow continues to be underrated in the eyes of both football fans and the betting market. The fact that they're rated lower than the two-loss Alabama Crimson Tide is proof of that. The Bruins' defense can carry them a long way this season, ranking fifth in opponent-adjusted EPA per play and second in opponent success rate. Much like Florida State vs. Pittsburgh, this is a game between one of the best defenses in the country and one of the worst. Illinois ranks 131st in defensive success rate, which has hurt them in several games already this season. I'll continue to ride with UCLA in this Big Ten game and bet on them to cover the double-digit spread. Pick: UCLA -10 (-108) Houston vs. Colorado Best Bet Colorado's defense is one-dimensional. They're ninth in the country in opponent EPA per rush, but they're 98th in opponent EPA per pass, meaning when they face a team that relies on an effective run game, the Buffaloes are in a great spot; but then they take on an elite passing attack, they struggle. Unfortunately for them, Houston has one of the best passing games in the country, ranking seventh in EPA per rush and fourth in pass success rate. That, paired with the fact that Colorado has one of the worst offenses in power conference football, leaves Houston in a great spot to cover as road favorites. headlines Friday night, with our college football expert backing the Illini to hang tough against a sputtering, injury-riddled UCLA offensive line. Photo By - Reuters Connect. Illinois vs UCLA Predictions Unbeaten UCLA (-9. 5) puts its perfect season on the line under the Rose Bowl lights tonight against 6-3 Illinois. My Illinois vs. UCLA prediction backs Bret Bielema's battle-tested Illini as a live underdog, with a physical, defense-first script dictating my full college football picks . FOX has live coverage of this contest at 9 p.m. ET on Friday, Nov. 13. TOP PICK Who will win Illinois vs UCLA: Illinois +9.5 Sell high on UCLA and take Illinois at +8.5 or better. The Bruins are 9-0 ATS and are running away with the Big Ten, but that doesn't mean they're a juggernaut. No single result on their resume is something Bret Bielema's squad isn't also capable of pulling off, so these teams are therefore still in a similar tier. UCLA's offense has stalled, ranking 86th in success rate and 133rd in explosiveness since Week 6 . That concern is exacerbated after starting tackle Hall Schmidt and starting center Riley Robell left the Minnesota game with injuries. Illinois has the better offense, checking in at 39th in EPA per play and 33rd in explosiveness over that span, and is therefore an appealing two-score underdog. Illinois vs UCLA Over/Under pick: Under 48.5 In a wet, rainy, short-week game, I'm betting on sloppy offensive results. UCLA's defense has been utter nails, leading the nation in EPA per play since Week 6. Sahir West (7.5 TFLs) is a terror on the edge, and linebacker Sammy Omosigho has played his way into high NFL Draft pick status as the Big Ten's highest-graded defender (92.0) at any position per PFF. Illinois' defense has experienced a revival since coordinator Bobby Hauck was fired. The secondary is a strength, featuring a wealth of experience, and a green front seven has drastically improved since the start of the season. Neither team will push the tempo, leading to a leisurely pace and offenses that rely on sustained drives. The Bruins rank 125th in seconds per snap (29.2), preferring to slowly drain the life out of opponents, and the Illini aren't far ahead at 90th (27.4). Illinois vs UCLA prop: First half Under 23.5 With the weather, Illinois' cross-country travel on a short week, and UCLA's defensive-first philosophy, this contest should start slow. The Bruins are 1-5 O/U against the first-half total in their last six home games, relying on a salty defense that makes life miserable for opposing offenses. The Illini are used to slow starts, averaging 18.4 total points in the first half in their last five games while exceeding 23.5 points just once. Illinois vs UCLA combo It's difficult to create margin in low-scoring games, so an Illinois cover correlates well with a low-scoring game. The Bruins haven't reached 5.7 yards per play or better in four of their last five games. A lack of offensive firepower and a suddenly listless rushing attack will show through. UCLA QB Ty Dieffenbach says first-half shoulder injury vs. Illinois not serious - ABC7 Los Angeles 24/7 Live Los Angeles Orange County Inland Empire Ventura County California SPORTS Share PASADENA, Calif. -- UCLA starting quarterback Ty Dieffenbach exited just before halftime because of a shoulder injury Friday but returned in the third quarter to lead the No. 4 Bruins past Illinois 22-14 for their 10th win of the season, tying a program record last reached in 1998. With 35 seconds left in the first half and the Bruins driving, Dieffenbach was tackled after throwing the ball downfield and appeared to land awkwardly. After being examined by trainers, he stood and gingerly walked off the field with the help of two teammates. "I went down a little awkward on the tackle, and my arm got caught up," said Dieffenbach, who is also nursing an ankle injury. "It just got tight. It's nothing serious." Coach Bob Chesney confirmed that Dieffenbach's injury wasn't serious and said he landed awkwardly on his non-throwing arm and hurt his elbow. "At halftime, his shoes are off, and he's got no shoulder pads. I'm like, 'Yeah, get your shoes back on,'" Chesney said. "But we had to go make sure everything was good in there and he was ready to go." The former Cal Poly quarterback, who took over after Week 1 starter Nico Iamaleava suffered a season-ending injury against Oregon last month, has led UCLA to five wins in five starts and has thrown for 1,218 yards and eight touchdowns. On Friday, he had thrown for 168 yards and a touchdown before he was replaced by third-stringer Madden Iamaleava , Nico's brother. Madden Iamaleava had one pass attempt all season and went 0-for-2 before the first half ended. The Bruins led the Illini 10-0 at the time. In the second half, with Dieffenbach still being evaluated, Madden Iamaleava led two drives that ended in a punt and a turnover on downs. By the time Dieffenbach emerged from the locker room to a loud ovation, UCLA was only up 12-7. "One of the best moments of my life hearing that crowd," Dieffenbach said. Ty Dieffenbach injury updates: UCLA QB returns after exiting in first half after hard hit - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College football winners/losers Texas ends LSU's playoff hopes Jordan Mendoza, USA TODAY · USA TODAY Sports Sat, November 14, 2026 at 3:53 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads PASADENA, CA — UCLA quarterback Ty Dieffenbach suffered an injury on a hard hit late in the first half against Illinois on Friday, Nov. 13. But it appears to not be an absolutely devastating hit for the Bruins . With 35 seconds left in the second quarter, Dieffenbach tried to throw the ball away when he got tripped up and was clearly in immediate pain. He was visibly shaken as he was attended to by support staff, and he appeared to indicate he had a left shoulder injury. After a few minutes he was helped up and taken to the sideline. Once the teams headed to the locker room, Dieffenbach went in appearing to not move his left arm and was limping. Ty Dieffenbach latest injury news Dieffenbach suffered an "upper body injury," according to the Fox broadcast. However, he emerged from the locker room with about four minutes left in the third quarter with a sleeve on his left arm, as the Rose Bowl crowd cheered. Dieffenbach was back on the field for UCLA late in the third quarter and played the remainder of the game. "I kind of went down a little awkward on the tackle, and my arm got caught up underneath, but it just got a little tight on me, and it's nothing serious," he said postgame. The Bruins got their quarterback to engineer another win. He reignited the offense, throwing a key fourth quarter touchdown to Semaj Morgan that strengthened the lead. UCLA held on to beat Illinois 22-14 to move to 10-0. Dieffenbach went 13-for-20 for 232 yards with two touchdowns and one interception, with 28 rushing yards. The injury was a big scare to UCLA's quarterback room as Dieffenbach has played in place of starter Nico Iamaleava after Iamaleava suffered a season ending injury against Oregon on Oct. 10. Dieffenbach has stepped up and kept the Bruins one of two undefeated teams left in the country, at 9-0 for the first time since 1998 with a shot at their first College Football Playoff appearance. Prior to the injury, Dieffenbach was 8-for-13 for 168 yards with one touchdown and one interception, leading UCLA to a 10-0 lead over Illinois. home.headline: UCLA endures injury scare, gets heroic return to stay unbeaten
home.blurb: It was a heroic return for the veteran who had departed UCLA’s game against Illinois just before halftime with a sore elbow and ankle. The crowd serenaded Dieffenbach with cheers anew once he came onto the field with his team holding a suddenly precarious lead over Illinois. All Dieffenbach did upon his return was to complete each of his five passes on the next drive, including a beautiful touchdown toss, to help the fourth-ranked Bruins hold on for a 22-14 victory that kept their unbeaten record intact. “That’s leadership, that stands out,” Chesney said, “and there’s the confidence everybody gained from that.” Illinois closed to within 19-14 after quarterback Katin Houser converted a huge fourth-down play, finding wide receiver Collin Dixon in the back of the end zone for a 7-yard touchdown with 7:14 left. But the Fighting Illini could conjure no more late magic after Houser went out with his own injury. “When we walked out there, I was like, damn, yes,” Chesney said of the crowd. “I knew we were on the brink of it and you were worried about the weather, but ultimately what a great job by them and really proud of the way they showed up.” After taking a shot in the arm, Ty Dieffenbach delivered one. Roars accompanied the previously injured UCLA quarterback with each step he took as he jogged back from the locker room to the Rose Bowl sideline late in the third quarter Friday night. “That crowd reaction was unbelievable,” Dieffenbach would say later. “I mean, that was one of the best moments of my life.” “They just don’t give up, they just don’t,” UCLA coach Bob Chesney said of his players. “They just believe they have a shot to win every game and they’re going to find a way.” The Bruins could exhale only after an Illinois pass fell incomplete over the middle with 43 seconds left. UCLA had registered another big defensive play only minutes earlier when safety Scooter Jackson came up with an interception – his second of the game – and returned it 41 yards to the Illinois 19-yard line with 2 minutes 42 seconds left. A short Mateen Bhaghani field goal gave the Bruins a 22-14 lead, necessitating a desperation drive by the Fighting Illini that came up well short. There were feel-good vibes all around after Dieffenbach escaped injury and UCLA improved to 10-0 for the first time since 1998 – the last season it won a conference championship. “No one believed that UCLA would be 10-0 this year, no one in the country, no one anywhere,” linebacker Sammy Omosigho said, “and we had to make them believe.” The Bruins, who are 7-0 in Big Ten games, need only one more victory in their final two regular-season games – against Michigan and USC – to clinch an appearance in the conference title game. Among other things, a season-high crowd of 45,800 celebrated a UCLA defense that intercepted three passes and registered five tackles for loss while holding the Fighting Illini (6-4, 4-3) to 240 yards of offense. picks.blurb: 2026 Week 11 Preview: Wake Forest Demon Deacons @ SMU Mustangs | Underdog Dynasty Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Rest of the FBS Community Underdog Dynasty November 15, 2026 Underdog Dynasty Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Conference USA Sun Belt Conference American Athletic Conference Betting FanDuel College Football Odds College Football Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Conference USA Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications ACC Wake Forest is rolling toward the ACC title game. But SMU, which has never lost a home ACC game, can stay in the race. Time and date: Saturday, November 14 at 12:00 p.m. ET Network: ESPN Location: Gerald J. Ford Stadium — Dallas, TX Spread: SMU (-1.5) Over/under: 61.5 All-time series: SMU leads, 3-1 Last meeting: Wake Forest 13, SMU 12 — October 25, 2025 Current streak: Wake Forest, 1 (2025) Setting the scene This might be the ACC regular season game of the year. For the first time in College Football Playoff history, the ACC champion is guaranteed an automatic bid. Thus, just getting access to Charlotte keeps the door ajar for Wake Forest and SMU in this high-stakes conference showdown. The Demon Deacons are one of the hottest teams in college football, winning six consecutive games, primarily in blowout fashion. But the Mustangs haven’t ever lost an matchup at Gerald J. Ford Stadium, faring 12-0 in their previous contests. A Wake Forest win propels the Demon Deacons to the doorstep of the ACC Championship Game. An SMU win creates chaos, bringing a cluster of 2-loss teams back into championship consideration, including itself. The ACC races greatly hinges on what unfolds Saturday afternoon on The Hilltop. Wake Forest Demon Deacons outlook Wake Forest (8-1, 5-1 ACC) is ranked No. 13 by the College Football Playoff committee, situated as the second-highest ACC team. Since its lone September loss to Miami (FL), the Demon Deacons have been as dominant as anyone in the FBS. During the last five games of its six-game win streak, Wake Forest has defeated opponents by an aggregate score of 264-31, or an average of 53-6 per game. The Demon Deacons used a dominant defense to stun SMU 13-12 in last year’s meeting in Winston-Salem, but this season, the offense has hit its stride under second-year coordinator Rob Ezell. Wake Forest ranks fourth nationally in scoring (43.3 points per game), ninth in total offense, and 10th in passing. Starting quarterback Gio Lopez missed last week’s game against FCS Merrimack with a lower body injury, but the absence was permissible due to the level of opponent. The former South Alabama and North Carolina gunslinger has been phenomenal in his new home, delivering 18 touchdowns against one interception this year, ranking 13th nationally in passing average. His mobility has made defenses pay too, accumulating 317 rushing yards and six touchdowns on the season. Lopez’s top target Carlos Hernandez is receiving national recognition. The senior is sixth in the FBS with an average of 105 receiving yards per game, and he regularly strikes from distance. Hernandez has multiple 70-yard touchdowns this season, and he has four outings with at least 110 yards and an end zone appearance. Jack Foley, Kam Shanks, and Antonio Meeks have provided support in this dynamic aerial attack, and the diversity in options allows Wake Forest to have the nation’s ninth-most efficient third down offense. The run game has been serviceable, ranking 43rd nationally in yards per game, while producing 4.94 yards per carry. Ty Clark and Deuce Lawrence have split carries throughout the season, totaling 416 and 327 rushing yards, respectively. Wake Forest’s offensive improvement has somewhat obscured the consistent impact of its defense. The Demon Deacons have only surrendered multiple scores once in their past five games, and they’ve finished 22 consecutive quarters without allowing more than seven points. The result is the country’s 13th-ranked scoring defense and 24th-ranked total defense — a unit which is particularly stingent against the run, surrendering just 85 yards per game on a 2.69 average. Defensive end Langston Hardy is the leader of the run-stuffing effort. He leads all ACC players with 13.5 tackles for loss, while also producing 44 tackles and 5.5 sacks. Backfield pressure has been a signature of this Wake Forest defense, and two other defensive linemen — Gabe Kirschke and Zach Lohavichan — have at least 7.5 tackles for loss. Wake Forest’s defense found the sustainable method of success, and that’s getting stops. The Demon Deacons are fifth nationally in both red zone defense and fourth down defense, finding ways to get off the field in critical situations. The unit can become even more dangerous if it dabbles in the turnover game. Wake Forest has forced just seven takeaways all season, which is tied for the eighth-fewest in the FBS. SMU Mustangs outlook SMU (7-2, 5-2 ACC) prepares for a revenge game against Wake Forest. Had the Mustangs prevailed last October in Winston-Salem, they would have competed in the ACC Championship Game with a College Football Playoff spot on the line. Instead, they fell in a 13-12 heartbreaker on a last-second field goal — one of the program’s four ACC losses since joining the conference in 2024. Zero of those losses transpired at Gerald J. Ford Stadium. SMU has been a different beast at home, and that was evident in its most complete game of the season last Friday against Virginia Tech. Counting games against FBS opponents, the Mustangs registered a season-high 23 first half points, utilizing its strongest start of the season to push past the Hokies, 51-28. The concept of senior day might have lost some luster in the transfer portal era, but Saturday will feature one of the most emotional senior day moments in recent memory. Kevin Jennings is in his fifth year with the program and third as the starting quarterback, and the Dallas area native has poured a lot into the program. Jennings guided the Mustangs to an American Conference title, an ACC Championship Game appearance, a College Football Playoff berth, and a Holiday Bowl victory. Now he’ll play his final game in Dallas, entering the pivotal matchup fifth nationally with 2,764 passing yards and fourth with 25 touchdown passes. The most remarkable part of Jennings’ eye-popping stats is his efficiency. For a quarterback that slings it deep quite often, the senior boasts a 73.9 completion rate, which is second among all players with at least 100 attempts. Jennings has also limited interceptions this year, finishing four of his last five starts without one. SMU’s high-powered passing attack involves a slew of receivers. Yamir Knight, coming off a 103-yard, 3-touchdown performance, is the most frequented with a team-high 50 catches. But Yannick Smith, Jalen Cooper, and Jalen Hale are also heavily involved — especially on downfield attempts — and all three average over 15.0 yards per reception this season. Tight ends Randy Pittman Jr. and Theo Melin Öhrström are also regular targets, tied for second on the team with four touchdown receptions apiece. The Mustangs’ run game is statistically a middle-of-the-road unit, ranked 70th in yards per game and 66th in rushing average. Kendrick Raphael operates as the top option, and he’s scored in seven of nine contests this year. Freshman Christian Rhodes has seen an increasing number of reps since mid-October, and he’s coming off a career-high 92 rushing yards against Virginia Tech. On defense, SMU displays a similar identity to the previous Mustang defenses of the Rhett Lashlee era: defensive line dominance. The Mustangs are one of 17 programs racking up at least 3.0 sacks per game, and defensive end Marques White is the ringleader of the movement. The eighth-year senior notched his third multi-sack game of the season last week, contributing to the turnover battle with a forced fumble and fumble recovery on the same play. But unlike the previous two seasons, SMU isn’t collecting turnovers on a consistent basis. The Mustangs have forced just eight turnovers all year, recovering five fumbles and picking off two passes. Despite the lack of takeaways, the secondary has shown considerable improvement from 2025, skyrocketing from 135th to 42nd in passing yards allowed per game, with safeties Jimmy Wyrick and Sael Reyes playing significant roles in that progress. Last year’s matchup between SMU and Wake Forest was the ultimate defensive battle. Just two touchdowns were scored — one on a 14-play drive and another capping a 41-yard series. There were eight combined turnovers in the matchup, which was decided on Connor Calvert’s 50-yard field goal as time expired. This year’s rematch looks bound to lean more on the higher-scoring end. Wake Forest brings significantly more offensive firepower in this matchup, headlined by the strong connection between Gio Lopez and Carlos Hernandez. The Demon Deacons’ offense has been virtually unstoppable since the start of October, and while SMU should provide some resistance with a formidable defensive line, Wake Forest will still get its points in Dallas. However, SMU can thrive in a shootout style game. The Mustangs are one of the most explosive offenses in the country, ranking ninth in the FBS with 15 plays spanning 40 yards. Wake Forest has excelled at preventing the big play this year, but the Mustangs’ receiving corps should present challenges on the back end that the Demon Deacons haven’t seen since the Miami (FL) loss. This back-and-forth thriller will come down to crunch time. With the backing of its home crowd, SMU improves to 13-0 in ACC matchups at Gerald J. Ford Stadium — a result which will add significant chaos to the final two weeks of ACC play. Betting odds slightly favor SMU, but the prediction favors Wake Forest in a high-scoring game. Week 11 of the College Football season gets us closer to the precipice of championship weekend. The ACC has a great slate to end the season, and Week 11 features a ton of awesome games. The showstopper is on at Noon ET, with the Wake Forest Demon Deacons taking on the SMU Mustangs. Wake Forest (8-1) has looked the part of a championship contender. There aren't a ton of takeaways from their 76-0 win against Merrimack out of the Football Championship Subdivision (FCS), but it continues a trend of dominance for them. The Demon Deacons. They haven't been within one score of a team since their upset win against Louisville earlier in the season, winning by 20+ in all of the past five matchups and 40+ in three of their past five matchups. SMU (7-2) should be closer to the ACC championship than they are. They proved it with a dominating 51-28 win against then 6-2 Virginia Tech, where their offense scored on nine of their 11 possessions. However, they dropped an easy game against Syracuse on Halloween. They lost 30-27, giving up a last-minute touchdown drive. That's been the only holdup preventing them from being in Wake Forest's spot. If you are looking for some betting advice for the matchup, we've got you covered. If anyone's expecting the 13-12 defensive bout we got last year, throw that out the window. This should be a shootout. Both teams possess some of the best quarterbacks in the nation, with Gio Lopez and Kevin Jennings combining for 4,940 yards, 43 touchdowns, and seven interceptions. They're the biggest reason why either team is at the place it is now. Wake Forest has a few advantages, though. The Demon Deacons are one of the top teams in the nation at stopping the run, allowing just 82.9 yards per game (No. 5 in the country). The Mustangs are slightly above average against the run (133.9 yards per game, No. 45). The Demon Deacons are also favorites in the turnover battle. They're one of the most turnover-averse teams in the country (0.4 giveaways per game, No. 2 in the country), while the Mustangs are pretty turnover-prone (1.5 giveaways per game, No. 95). This game should have no problem hitting the over, with both of these teams boasting some of the top passing offenses in the league. However, give me the Demon Deacons in a road win. With bowl eligibility still in question, Mike Elko's squad will welcome one of the nation's top-ranked teams to Kyle Field for its annual Operation: Blackout game. Texas A&M enters the matchup looking to build momentum after an inconsistent season that has featured significant offensive struggles. Despite sitting at 4-5, the Aggies have shown flashes of defensive promise, allowing 20 points or fewer in five games this season. Meanwhile, Tennessee arrives in College Station following a dominant victory over Kentucky. The Volunteers have one of the nation's most dangerous pass defenses, leading the FBS with 39 sacks. However, with the home crowd behind them and plenty to play for, the Aggies have an opportunity to pull off an upset. Here are three bold predictions for Texas A&M against Tennessee. Texas A&M Holds DeSean Bishop Under 75 Rushing Yards Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop has been one of the Volunteers' most productive offensive weapons this season, averaging 118.4 rushing yards per game with 13 touchdowns. However, Texas A&M's defense will make stopping Bishop its top priority. With Tennessee losing backup running back Daune Morris for the remainder of the season, the Volunteers will likely depend even more heavily on Bishop. That could give Elko and defensive coordinator Jay Bateman an opportunity to load the box and force quarterback Joey Aguilar to win through the air. The Aggies have demonstrated the ability to keep opposing offenses under control, and Saturday could be another example. Prediction: Bishop finishes with fewer than 75 rushing yards and no touchdowns. 2. Marcel Reed Accounts for Three Touchdowns Without a Turnover Texas A&M quarterback Marcel Reed has struggled with consistency this season, particularly against ranked opponents. With eight interceptions, protecting the football will be critical against a Tennessee defense that thrives on creating pressure. However, Tennessee's biggest defensive weakness could provide Reed with an opportunity. The Volunteers have struggled against mobile quarterbacks, and Reed has the athleticism to exploit those problems. His performance against Arkansas, when he rushed for 66 yards and a touchdown on nine carries, showed what he can accomplish when the Aggies utilize his legs. Texas A&M enters the contest 4-5 overall and 1-5 in SEC play following a frustrating 17-9 loss to South Carolina. Despite finishing with 457 total yards against the Gamecocks, the Aggies struggled to finish drives, failing to score a touchdown despite several opportunities inside South Carolina territory. Tennessee enters Saturday's matchup 7-2 overall and 4-2 in conference play following an impressive 34-6 victory over Kentucky. The Volunteers have won two of their last three games, including victories over Alabama and Kentucky, but their recent struggles away from Knoxville could give Texas A&M an opportunity. The Aggies will need another strong defensive performance, particularly against Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop, who has surpassed 1,000 rushing yards this season. Offensively, quarterback Marcel Reed must find ways to sustain drives and avoid the mistakes that have plagued Texas A&M throughout conference play. Tennessee enters Saturday as a 2.5-point favorite , and most national experts are picking the Volunteers. However, at least one analyst believes Texas A&M can pull off the upset at home. Here is who the experts and prediction models are picking to win Saturday's matchup: Bill Connelly – ESPN SP+: Tennessee David Kenyon – Bleacher Report: Tennessee Pete Fiutak – College Football News: Tennessee Jake Margolick – College Football News: Texas A&M ESPN Analytics: Tennessee with a 58.6% win probability For Texas A&M, Saturday presents an opportunity to earn its first victory over a ranked opponent this season and take another step toward bowl eligibility. The Aggies must win two of their final three games to reach six victories, making the remaining schedule increasingly important. Tennessee leads the all-time series 3-2 and won the most recent meeting 20-13 in Knoxville in 2023. However, Texas A&M won the Volunteers' last trip to Kyle Field, securing a memorable 45-38 double-overtime victory in 2016. Saturday's matchup kicks off at 2 p.m. CT on ESPN. Mandatory Credit: Gary Cosby Jr.-Tuscaloosa News | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Noah Ruiz · Texas A&M On SI Fri, November 13, 2026 at 8:16 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads With just three more games to reach bowl eligibility, Texas A&M football is in desperate need of its first ranked win of the season. Despite having one of the Southeastern Conference's best home-field advantages, it won't be an easy task against one of the top-ranked defenses in the country in Tennessee . Entering the matchup with the Aggies, the Volunteers have 39 sacks, the most in all of college football and haven't allowed more than 27 points this season. On the flip side, quarterback Marcel Reed and his offense have scored at most 2 touchdowns against Power 4 opponents in the past month. To make matters worse, the Aggies became the first team in college football history to have over 450 yards, zero turnovers, and fail to score a touchdown in their latest loss to South Carolina. With those facts in mind, will the Maroon and White find a way to reverse their fortune, or will their matchup against the Volunteers be more of the same bland offense that has shown up for the better part of nine games? The two schools haven't met at Kyle Field in 10 years, when the Aggies won a wild double-overtime thriller, but let's see what the staff of Texas A&M Aggies on SI have to say about the outcome of this one. Staff Predictions for Tennessee at Texas A&M Sep 19, 2026; College Station, Texas, USA; Texas A&M Aggies defensive tackle DJ Hicks (5) tackles Kentucky Wildcats running back CJ Baxter (1) during the third quarter at Kyle Field. Mandatory Credit: Maria Lysaker-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Aggies' offense is no match for Tennessee's vaunted defense as Texas A&M fails to score a touchdown (again). Also, I seriously can't believe the spread on this game. The gambling lords in the desert don't understand vibes. Tennessee 21, A&M 6 The last time the Aggies hosted a conference opponent at Kyle Field, they were victorious over the Arkansas Razorbacks, one of the lower-tier teams in the SEC. Marcel Reed has shown improvement in his play over the past two games, but Tennessee's defense is going to be his biggest test, and Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop will give A&M's run defense a run for their money as well. But A&M's run defense has shown their stinginess against prime running backs, and scoring in the red zone this year against A&M's defense is an impressive feat to pull off. If they can keep that rolling against the Vols, then SEC win number two is well within range for the Maroon and White, especially if George MacIntyre is starting. A&M could be P.O.ed just enough to make that happen. A&M 28, Tennessee 24 It's hard to have confidence in the Aggies offense, and it's even tougher to believe in them going against one of the best defenses in the country. The Volunteers should take advantage of a team playing uninspired football and handle business. Tennessee 31, A&M 10 Kolton Becker A&M needs this game to avoid having to win the next two games to become bowl-eligible. Does that mean it can happen? We'll find out more Saturday, but a lot of the numbers indicate that Tennessee's defense and offense should be able to take care of business. I think that happens. Tennessee 38, A&M 30 Two great defenses, one miserable offense. But a blind squirrel finds a nut once in a while. Maybe with a cold breeze, this will be the time. Again, Texas A&M is a bad football team with way more questions than answers, and with three games remaining, the pressure continues to mount on third-year coach Mike Elko . Will the coaching staff change during the season? That remains to be seen, and after making his ninth start, senior quarterback Marcel Reed isn't expected to be benched. While Reed played better, completing 25-of-43 for 251 yards, Texas A&M failed to score a touchdown for the third time in SEC play, and is reportedly the first team to produce over 450 yards without a touchdown, adding more insult to injury to a season that has been lost for quite some time. away.headline: Tennessee football QB George MacIntyre injury update from Josh Heupel
away.blurb: Texas A&M safety Chance Collins, who's a true freshman, tackled MacIntyre as he was attempting to make a throw to Braylon Staley with 12:43 left in the third quarter. MacIntyre got the throw off as he got hit, but it flew out of bounds. He's dealing with a right knee injury, according to the ESPN broadcast, and was wearing a knee brace when he came out of the tent a second time to throw on the sidelines. MacIntyre did not return to the game the next drive, and freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon entered the game the next drive with 7:39 left in the third. MacIntyre was jogging in place on the sidelines and testing his knee with Brandon in the game. Tennessee football quarterback George MacIntyre suffered an apparent injury during the third quarter of the road matchup with Texas A&M after getting hit hard on a third down. The sophomore quarterback limped off the field with Tennessee punting on fourth down, and he headed to the medical tent. MacIntyre returned to the field on the Vols' next drive, but then returned to the medical tent during Texas A&M's following drive. The No. 9 Vols won 22-7 at Kyle Field. "George got twisted up on the one-pass play," Tennessee coach Josh Heupel said after the game. "Comes back in and was battling through it and had to go back. Just with where the game was and what we felt like we needed. It didn't feel like it was the right place for George, just dealing with that injury, so that's why Faizon was in there at that time. Both of them played extremely well. Proud of both of those guys. Big smiles on their faces, excited about the win." Tennessee trailed the Aggies 7-6 when MacIntyre left the game. MacIntyre completed 13 of his 17 passes for 109 yards before the hit. Brandon completed his only pass for a 5-yard touchdown. He had six carries for 36 yards. MacIntyre has completed 91 of 134 passes this season for 962 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions. home.headline: Injury update on Daevin Hobbs for Tennessee football vs Texas A&M
home.blurb: Hobbs had recorded 12 tackles and 2.5 tackles for loss in eight games prior to the injury. The Vols are facing depth issues on the defensive line, having already lost Tyree Weathersby for the season. Tennessee football defensive lineman Daevin Hobbs went to the medical tent midway through the first half of its game at Texas A&M on Nov. 14, but returned to the lineup for the second half. Hobbs limped off the field under his own power during Texas A&M's first drive of the second quarter. He went to the medical tent to be examined by athletic training staff. But he was on the field for Tennessee's first defensive series after halftime. The No. 9 Vols trailed Texas A&M 7-6 when Hobbs left the game. Going into the Texas A&M game, Hobbs had logged 12 total tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss and 4 quarterback hits in eight appearances. He made one tackle before exiting the game vs. the Aggies. Depth along the defensive line is becoming an issue for the Vols, who already lost Tyree Weathersby , the team leader in sacks with seven, to a season ending knee injury in the win over Kentucky on Nov. 7. Star lineman Xavier Gilliam left the game briefly in the first half but returned soon after. Stephen Thompson covers Tennessee Volunteers men's basketball. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings The reigning national champion and ninth-ranked Hoosiers look to avoid a potentially devastating second loss when they host No. 18 USC Getty Images No. 9 Indiana is feeling the heat for its Big Ten showdown with No. 18 USC on Saturday after falling five spots in the College Football Playoff rankings during its bye week. But the Hoosiers, who have yet to announce a starting quarterback for the game, can calm the waters by notching a quality win over the visiting Trojans. USC is lagging outside the CFP picture…for now. That will change if the Trojans can upset IU on the road after beating Ohio State in their last game during Week 9. A win would also catapult USC into the Big Ten title race, revitalizing a season that appeared to be in peril after a 24-7 loss at Wisconsin on Oct. 24. The question is which Indiana quarterback the Trojans will be tasked with defending. Season-long starter Josh Hoover injured his throwing arm during Indiana's Week 9 win over Minnesota and was benched after subsequent struggles. Veteran backup Grant Wilson entered and completed 9 of 17 passes for 156 yards and a touchdown, sparking a quarterback controversy. Hoosiers coach Curt Cignetti was noncommittal this week on who will take the first snaps for IU, forcing USC to be ready for either option. The situation has created some late-season intrigue for the reigning national champions, who have been unable to pull away from most of their Big Ten opponents during an 8-1 (5-1 Big Ten) start. Where to watch USC vs. Indiana live Date : Saturday, Nov. 14 | Time : 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Memorial Stadium -- Bloomington, Indiana TV: CBS | Live stream: CBSSports.com , CBS Sports App Streaming on Paramount+ Premium USC vs. Indiana: Need to know Can USC match Indiana's physicality?: Regardless of who is at quarterback for Indiana, USC's defense will have its hands full with the Hoosiers' skill talent. Physical receivers Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh comprise one of the best 1-2 tandems in college football. Meanwhile, IU running backs Turbo Richard and Lee Beebe Jr . are both averaging more than five yards per carry and are over 700 yards each for the season. USC has never been known for its physicality under coach Lincoln Riley, but keeping the Hoosiers in check will require it. Going on the road and winning against a team with Indiana's gritty DNA wouldn't just be a huge boost for the Trojans' playoff aspirations; it would also help change the perception of Riley's program. Indiana's CFP outlook: Indiana's chances of making the playoff will reach near "lock" status at 96.2% with a win, according to the CBS Sports CFP Forecaster. An Oct. 10 win over Nebraska is not aging well, as the Cornhuskers are on a four-game losing streak. After that, IU's best win is either on the road against a 5-4 Michigan team or at home against a 6-3 Northwestern team. However you slice it, the Hoosiers don't have a win against a team currently ranked in the CFP Top 25. Beating USC would change that...assuming the Trojans remain in the rankings. USC's CFP outlook: This is do-or-die for USC's playoff hopes. The Trojans' chances of making the field will rise to 51.5% with a win and plummet to 3.7% with a loss. In other words, the playoff has already started for Lincoln Riley's team. It's really a simple formula: finish 3-0 with wins over Indiana, Maryland and USC, and the Trojans will unquestionably make the playoff for the first time. Lose any of those games, and it's probably over for what is arguably the most historic program to have never appeared in the CFP. USC vs. Indiana prediction, picks Five of Indiana's six Big Ten games have been decided by a touchdown or less. The only exception was a 47-15 win against an overmatched Rutgers team. The Hoosiers haven't shown the ability to pull away and dominate quality opposition. So long as IU limits catastrophic turnovers, it will win the game on the basis of its physicality on both lines of scrimmage. But it's difficult to envision the Hoosiers suddenly pulling away from a team of USC's caliber. The Trojans have a veteran quarterback in Jayden Maiava who can keep his team in the game. With the College Football Playoff and conference championship pictures getting clearer by the week, we have plenty of high-stakes action on Saturday. It begins on Saturday, as the No. 13 Wake Forest Demon Deacons take on the SMU Mustangs in an ACC clash with plenty of postseason implications. Then, we'll move to the Big Ten, where the No. 9 Indiana Hoosiers look to prove the committee wrong when they host the No. 18 USC Trojans . To close it all out, we have a huge Big 12 battle between the No. 2 Utah Utes and No. 23 Arizona Wildcats . With so much to get to, let's dive into my college football picks and NCAAF predictions for the Week 11 games on Saturday, November 14. Wake Forest vs. SMU Prediction Wake Forest Demon Deacons Quarterback Gio Lopez was out for Wake Forest's most recent win, a 77-0 annihilation of Merrimack from the FCS. Head coach Jake Dickert stated that a lower-body injury suffered against Virginia in Week 9 was progressing and he's on the "right track" to see action against SMU. Lopez has been critical to the Demon Deacons' offensive success, a unit that ranks as the top overall scoring team in terms of Finishing Drives. Wake Forest has one of the highest numbers of offensive drives to cross the opponent's 40-yard line, averaging 5.1 points per trip. The surprising aspect of Wake Forest football comes on the defensive side, with the team ranking in the top 20 among all FBS teams in opponent Success Rate allowed, Quality Drives allowed and Defensive Finishing Drives. Opposing offenses have struggled to create explosive plays against coordinator Scottie Hazelton's defense. The Demon Deacons rank as the top defense nationally in allowing 20-yard plays from scrimmage . SMU recovered from a Week 9 loss at Syracuse with a rocking-chair victory over Virginia Tech . The Mustangs posted a 63% Success Rate on standard downs, leading to just 17 plays on passing downs. The explosive drive was the biggest variable for the offense, creating offensive possessions that averaged at least 10 yards per play on 4-of-11 drives. Quarterback Kevin Jennings had four pass-catchers average more than 10 yards per target, as Yamir Knight and Jalen Cooper combined for four touchdown s on more than 200 yards of receiving. The SMU defense continued to struggle in two key areas, as Virginia Tech averaged 6.7 yards per carry and cashed in with a touchdown on all three red-zone attempts. The Mustangs boast a top-25 pass-rush defense and fall within the top 40 of Havoc rankings, but the ability to get opposing offenses off schedule has been the challenge . SMU ranks 78th in standard downs Success Rate allowed compared to 20th in passing downs. Third-down defense has been immaculate for head coach Rhett Lashlee, ranking ninth in third-down defense. Wake Forest vs SMU Pick For SMU to climb into position for the ACC Championship game, the defense must step up on standard downs. Wake Forest elects to run the ball on 58% of first downs and just over 50% of second downs, placing emphasis on the run concepts. The Demon Deacons are a zone-read offense led by running back Ty Clark III. The junior has been lackluster in elusiveness, averaging just 2.7 yards after first contact while forcing only 13 missed tackles on the season. The SMU defense has a respectable 51% Success Rate against inside and outside zone, indicating that Wake Forest will need heroics from Lopez. SMU has fielded a much better pass defense than rush defense, ranking in the top 50 in EPA allowed. Lopez has high Success Rate numbers against SMU's preferred coverages of man, Cover 3 and Cover 1. The Mustangs' ability to generate pressure is key against Lopez, as the quarterback has failed to force a turnover-worthy play in a clean pocket. Wake Forest ranks 71st in pass blocking, an issue against SMU edge defender Marques White, who has seven sacks and 29 pressures on the season. Wake Forest will also be successful in sending the opposing offense into passing downs. SMU uses the zone-read run concept more than most teams in FBS, but the Demon Deacons have a high 57% Success Rate against it. The biggest advantage for Wake Forest in the advanced statistics is the elite numbers in allowing methodical drives and converting scoring opportunities into points . The Demon Deacons rank 13th in Quality Drives, defined as the ability to limit methodical possessions. SMU has struggled to get downfield all season without using explosives, ranking 89th in offensive momentum killer. Action Network's Betting Power Ratings have SMU slightly favored by a point, directly where the market resides. The bigger edge comes in the totals department with a projection of 55. SMU's heavy pass rush will create a crowded pocket for Lopez, as his turnover-worthy play rate rises to 3.4% with pressure. Conversely, SMU will struggle to sustain drives and enter scoring position against a Wake Forest defense that has been top-10 in points allowed in scoring position. Pete Fiutak · College Football News Thu, November 12, 2026 at 4:37 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Just when it seemed like USC was finished, and a new era would soon start with Lincoln Riley all but gone after an ugly 24-7 loss at Wisconsin, a funny thing happened – the Trojans rolled Ohio State 30-18. And now, at 7-2, with high-profile dates remaining against CFP No. 9 Indiana and No. 8 UCLA, No. 18 USC all but controls its own path to the CFP – a 10-2 Trojan team with two top-ten wins in the final three games wouldn't be a lock to get in, but … yeah, it would be. But Indiana is still pretty good. It's 8-1, this close to being 9-0, and even though the schedule hasn't been a killer, if it keeps winning, all will be just fine. But lose this, and the pressure will be on to avoid a slip over the last two weeks. USC vs Indiana: Quick Hits Indiana travels to Washington after this before finishing with the rivalry date against Purdue. USC hosts Maryland after this before the showdown at UCLA. It's just the fifth meeting ever, and the first since USC joined the Big Ten. The Trojans are 4-0, including the 1968 Rose Bowl. How To Watch USC vs Indiana Date: Saturday, November 14, 2026 Game Time: 3:30 PM ET TV: CBS Location: Memorial Stadium, Bloomington, IN – Week 11 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Bowl & CFP Projections | Top 25 – How many 3-loss CFP teams will there be? Why USC Will Win Plenty of things have to go right. USC has the punting to own the field position game, there can't be a slew of turnovers, and Indiana has to keep struggling. The only way to put it is that it's like the Hoosiers forgot how to score. The offense is moving a bit, but it hasn't scored more than 20 points in regulation since early October. The USC passing game continues to be good enough. The ground game might be hit-or-miss, but Jayden Maiava is a smart, tough veteran who keeps hitting his throws for the Big Ten's best offense on third downs. Why Indiana Will Win Indiana got a week off to reset at just the right time. No, it's not playing nearly as well offensively as it did last year. No, it doesn't have that dominant mode, and it certainly doesn't have the same passing game. And yet it's still 8-1 – this bunch finds ways to win. For all of the issues on offense, the defense continues to be outstanding. The run D is the fourth-best in the nation, allowing just 2.3 yards per carry overall with no touchdowns in the last three games. USC might throw well, but it wasn't all that long ago that the ground game was stuffed for -18 yards by Wisconsin. USC vs Indiana Prediction, Betting Lines Is Grant Wilson up to the gig, or will Josh Hoover get the nod as he fights through an injury? No matter who ends up under center, he'll be fine against a USC defense that's been hit hard by injuries. Indiana's offense – even without banged up star RB Turbo Richard – will be a bit more effective than it was against Ohio State, Michigan, or Minnesota, but it'll be the defensive front and run defense that keeps the good season going. away.headline: Indiana Makes Major QB Decision Ahead of No. 18 USC Showdown
away.blurb: Josh Hoover, who has started the first nine games, has been limited by injury in recent weeks. Wilson stepped in during the second half of IU's game vs. Minnesota "We'll see how the week plays out and we'll see who we trot out there," Cignetti said Monday, according to Indiana Athletics . Hoover's availability appeared to leave the door open for a return. Neither quarterback appeared on Saturday's Big Ten injury report. Indiana must also account for another loss on offense. Starting right guard Joe Brunner was ruled out after suffering an injury in practice Thursday, according to Zenitz . Running back Turbo Richard is also unavailable, so Wilson faces a tricky assignment against Lincoln Riley's Trojans. Indiana Makes Major QB Decision Ahead of No. 18 USC Showdown The Indiana Hoosiers are expected to make a quarterback change for one of their biggest games of the season. No. 9 Indiana is expected to start Grant Wilson over Josh Hoover against No. 18 USC on Saturday, Nov. 14, according to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz . Hoover started Indiana's first nine games but has battled an injury to his throwing arm in recent weeks. Wilson replaced him against Minnesota on Oct. 31 and helped the Hoosiers escape with an overtime victory. The reported decision comes despite Hoover being cleared to play against the Trojans. Indiana enters the matchup at 8-1, with its Big Ten title hopes and College Football Playoff position at stake. Indiana Expected to Start Grant Wilson Over Josh Hoover Getty BLOOMINGTON, INDIANA – APRIL 23: Grant Wilson #2 of the Indiana Hoosiers throws a pass during the 2026 Indiana Spring Football Game at Memorial Stadium on April 23, 2026 in Bloomington, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images for ONIT) Wilson made his case for the starting job during Indiana's 23-16 overtime victory over Minnesota. If Michigan has any chance to win this game, the Wolverines' offense has to come alive and establish the run . Here's how Michigan on SI sees the game going. Michigan still has one of the best defenses in the country and last week was a major disappointment by their standards — and they didn't even allow a touchdown. But five field goals were too much with how poorly the Wolverines' offense has played. Firing Jason Beck was the right move, but it was too late in the season. Michigan isn't going to have wholesale changes and I just don't see a way for the Wolverines to score enough points to win a game like this on the road. To see Kyle Whittingham, who had an esteemed career in Utah for 20 years, go out like this is upsetting. I just don't see how he stays on after this season. It's been madness. And seeing how he fired a guy he brought with him from Utah, offensive coordinator Jason Beck, midseason, it just feels like there's no order here. Because Beck is now gone, offensive line coach Jim Harding is taking over. The problem is, Harding hasn't called plays before, and Whittingham acknowledged that he's not going to be involved. So, would it have been better to just stick with Beck? Too late now. To Whittingham's defense, his offense had all the talent in the world, but zero execution. Quarterback Bryce Underwood was such a disaster that the Wolverines had to turn to Tommy Carr. Wide receiver JJ Buchanan is the only player worth anything, while running backs Savion Hiter and Jordan Marshall average under four yards per carry. So, would you be surprised, after telling you all that, that Michigan ranks 128th in standard down Success Rate and 109th in Havoc allowed? Of course you're not. Luckily for the Wolverines, the defense has been this team's saving grace. Defense has always been Whittingham's forte, so Michigan ranking 12th in the FBS, allowing an average of 16.2 points per game, is par for the course. The Wolverines have managed to stifle both the run and the pass, ranking in the top 10 in Success Rate allowed. Michigan followed in Oregon's footsteps because the Ducks fired their offensive coordinator, Drew Mehringer, a few weeks ago. The Ducks, who had National Championship aspirations this season, sank early on and lost their quarterback, Dante Moore , who suffered a concussion but is now saving himself for the NFL Draft. So, it's been Dylan Raiola taking over under center. Since Oregon fired Mehringer, assistant quarterbacks coach Jay Johnson has been calling plays, and his connection with Raiola has been palpable. Raiola's first action after Moore went so bad that third-string Brock Thomas started against Nebraska , but he ended up bouncing back. Raiola's main target has been Dakorien Moore, who's been generating a ton of volume, including a two- touchdown game with over 120 yards two weeks ago against Northwestern . We've also seen a major uptick in the run game. Jordon Davison is likely going to miss this game after hurting himself last week, but Dierre Hill Jr. has picked up the slack. At 5-4 and coming off an embarrassing 15-6 loss to Michigan State, Michigan desperately needs something positive. Unfortunately, that opportunity comes against No. 18 Oregon inside Autzen Stadium, one of the loudest and most intimidating venues in college football. The Ducks will have the benefit of a hostile home crowd, while Michigan will be breaking in a new offensive coordinator and attempting to find some semblance of consistency on that side of the ball. It's hardly an ideal combination. When Michigan Has The Ball All eyes will be on interim offensive coordinator Jim Harding , who takes over following Kyle Whittingham's decision to fire Jason Beck. Michigan enters the matchup ranked No. 126 nationally in scoring offense, No. 109 in rushing offense, No. 125 in passing offense and No. 132 in total offense. Those numbers are remarkably poor for a program with Michigan's resources and expectations. Whittingham hasn't officially named freshman Tommy Carr the starter, but all signs point to No. 14 manning the offense. Carr has shown flashes since replacing Bryce Underwood, but he's also operating behind an offensive line that has struggled throughout the season. Against Oregon, those protection issues could become even more glaring. The Wolverines need Jordan Marshall and Savion Hiter to establish something on the ground, particularly early. Otherwise, Carr could find himself facing obvious passing situations against an aggressive defense with the Autzen crowd making communication difficult. Harding doesn't need to reinvent the offense overnight. He needs to simplify things, establish manageable situations and give Carr opportunities to succeed. When Oregon Has The Ball Michigan's defense has been the more reliable unit by a mile, and that group will need another outstanding performance to keep this competitive. Defensive coordinator Jay Hill has enough talent to make things difficult, particularly with players like John Henry Daley, Zeke Berry, Chris Bracy and Jyaire Hill capable of creating disruptive plays. But Oregon presents a different challenge. The Ducks can put considerable pressure on a defense through tempo, athleticism, pure speed and offensive versatility. Michigan cannot afford repeated three-and-outs that force its defense to spend the afternoon on the field. If Oregon establishes an early lead, the Wolverines could find themselves in serious trouble. Michigan's defense should compete, but expecting Harding to completely transform one of America's worst offenses in less than a week is unrealistic. Autzen Stadium only makes matters worse. The Wolverines keep things respectable early before Oregon pulls away, leaving Michigan with two remaining opportunities to secure bowl eligibility. Oregon 27, Michigan 10

But what happens between the lines, with Oregon seeking to make an unexpected run at the College Football Playoff and Michigan seeking to bounce back from a brutal loss to Michigan State? Michigan playing without its two sack leaders would make a significant difference and perhaps allow the Ducks to break out for another big day. One player who is set to see an uptick in snaps is the dynamic Nasir Wyatt, though he is listed as probable as of Thursday evening so he may be banged up. picks.headline: Ole Miss vs. Oklahoma Predictions: Why our Staff is Split on the Winner
picks.blurb: Ole Miss vs. Oklahoma Predictions: Why our Staff is Split on the Winner Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3) is back on the road this weekend, where it will meet the Oklahoma Sooners (5-4, 3-3) in Norman for a game that each side could really use in the win column. For Oklahoma, it won’t mean much in terms of a playoff push, but it will go a long way in salvaging what’s been a lost season. The Sooners don’t have consecutive wins (or losses) on the season yet, but they have collected wins over Texas and Florida in the last five weeks. For Ole Miss, its CFP hopes are on thin ice and to even be somewhat involved in the conversation next month, the Rebels badly need to win their final three regular season games. Ole Miss initially opened as a 2.5-point road favorite last week, but will now enter the weekend as a narrow 1.5-point underdog. Ahead of the Rebels' latest conference matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Ole Miss On SI Staff Predictions Oklahoma Sooners quarterback John Mateer (10) runs beside Ole Miss Rebels linebacker Suntarine Perkins (4) during a college football game between the University of Oklahoma Sooners (OU) and the Ole Miss Rebels at Gaylord Family Ð Oklahoma Memorial Stadium in Norman, Okla., Saturday, Oct. 25, 2025. Ole Miss won 34-26. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Tyler Komis This weekend will mark another notable challenge for Ole Miss on the offensive side of the ball. It’s not an ideal weekend to not have Patrick Kutas available either, arguably Ole Miss’ top offensive lineman over the past two seasons. Oklahoma brings a defensive front that’s up to nearly 30 sacks on the year and one of the best run defenses in the conference, entering game day. Ole Miss desperately needs to bounce back in both departments, as it surrendered five sacks and ran for just 66 rushing yards in its loss last week. While there’s no doubt Ole Miss’ offensive line will get tested, and that Oklahoma will be sending consistent pressure, I’m picking Trinidad Chambliss to capitalize on what is looking like his final test against a great collegiate defense. Though Ole Miss will be without its leading tackler in Keaton Thomas, Oklahoma’s offense shouldn’t pose much of a threat anyway. It’s a golden opportunity for the Rebels to get right on that side of the ball. I expect a close game in Norman, thanks to the Sooners’ defense, but if one team was going to separate itself by multiple scores I think it would likely be Oklahoma. Ole Miss 27, Oklahoma 20 Matt Galatzan Ole Miss needs to get back on track if it is going to save its season. Fortunately, Oklahoma is the perfect opponent to do just that. The Sooners have struggled mightily this season, and the Rebels have the best quarterback in the country, and their backs against the wall. I think Ole Miss wins, and wins big. Unfortunately, I see the latter as more likely. I think Ole Miss' offense comes out flat, and the grocery list of injuries bites the Rebels in the back. I don't think the Rebel defense is strong enough to shut down Oklahoma's offense completely. I expect Oklahoma to weasel out a tight one. Oklahoma 23, Ole Miss 20 Coming off such an embarrassing loss to Georgia, I think Ole Miss bounces back this weekend against Oklahoma. I don’t think either team’s offense will be particularly strong on Saturday. However, I have more faith in Ole Miss’ offense to recover from a string of poor performances, even if Ole Miss linebacker Keaton Thomas is out and Jason Witten has taken over as the Sooners’ interim offensive coordinator and play-caller. Give me the Rebels by three points in a game defined by the two teams’ defenses. The Rebels have plenty of questions to answer offensively, especially with Kewan Lacy and Patrick Kutas out. Oklahoma’s defense is one of the toughest units in the SEC, and I expect Brent Venables to make life difficult for Trinidad Chambliss throughout the afternoon. However, I still have faith in Pete Golding’s defense to get the job done against an Oklahoma offense that is still trying to find its identity under Jason Witten. The Sooners looked better against Florida, but I need to see more before buying into the offensive turnaround. Ole Miss has too much at stake to let another opportunity slip away, and I expect Chambliss to lead a late scoring drive to secure a critical road victory. Ole Miss 24, Oklahoma 20 For Ole Miss, it comes down to scoring on the Sooners. Oklahoma lacks a sufficient run game, and at times, John Mateer can really struggle. If the Rebels lose, it will likely be because of that deadly defense. I predict that the Sooners defend their home territory and win 21-17 with a great defensive performance. I hope the Rebels prove me wrong, but they need to improve a lot, including their run game and tackling. The defense looks better, but the offense doesn’t do quite enough to defeat Oklahoma. picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for Ole Miss' Trip to Oklahoma
picks.source: Ole Miss Rebels On SI on MSN
picks.blurb: No team should be judged by how they perform when everything is going its way, just as this Ole Miss program should be judged on how it can respond after the tumult it faced last time out against Georgia. With the Rebels' playoff hopes dwindling to the lowest they have been all season, Pete Golding's squad will need to respond in a big way this afternoon in Norman . Facing an Oklahoma team with a retooled offensive scheme and rejuvenated belief in itself, Ole Miss will need to capitalize on the trend that the Sooners have yet to win consecutive games this season. Just about everything went wrong at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium last weekend for the Rebels, and it's true; everyone has a plan until they get punched in the face. Golding's side took a clean hit to the jaw from the Bulldogs, and Ole Miss will need to claw itself up against Oklahoma if it wants a chance at getting back to the playoffs this season. Trinidad Chambliss Plays a Clean Game Following His Worst Showing Numbers talk, and for Trinidad Chambliss, they're quite damning. Throwing nine passes to the wrong side this season, the Rebels' former Heisman frontrunner is third in the Football Bowl Subdivision for interceptions this year. If Ole Miss wants to win on the road tomorrow and show that it can play in tough road environments, Chambliss will need to clean the turnovers up. The differences between Georgia and Oklahoma are clear, and I truly believe that Chambliss will return to the form he got fans used to in the 2025 season. The Rebels need their star to play a professional game today, and that all starts with taking care of the ball and making the right decisions when the Sooner pass rush gets in his way. The days of Chambliss and Kewan Lacy backfields are over this year, and the former will need to remind the Rebels' faithful of the leader he is capable of being. Behind a reworked offensive line, I expect Chambliss to erase the doubts that have been growing surrounding him recently, and #6 will lead Ole Miss to victory in Norman on the heels of a strong offensive showing. Shekai Mills-Knight has the Best Rushing Performance of the Season While Lacy's legacy in Oxford looks like it will end full of questions about injuries and unfulfilled potential, the Rebels have a tailback capable of reshaping the team's rushing narrative late in the season. I wholeheartedly believe in Ole Miss' French-Canadian sophomore, and John David Baker's offensive scheming needs to rely on the talent that can line up beside Chambliss. Shekai Mills-Knight, when utilized by Baker, has been a revelation for Ole Miss' rushing attack; the only issue is that Knight has been used nowhere near enough. Makhi Frazier has left a lot to be desired since arriving at Ole Miss from Michigan State, and with Knight receiving the leftover touches, the Rebels have seen what the sophomore back is capable of. If Shekai Mills-Knight is given an uptick in touches in Norman, there is no reason that the tailback cannot eclipse Ole Miss' single-game leading rusher this season: Kewan Lacy's 122-yard showing against Missouri. The Rebels need to be more dynamic offensively, and it all starts with feeding the Canadian native. The Defense Holds Oklahoma Under 21 Georgia's offense was able to do whatever it wanted in Oxford last weekend, and the Rebels will need to suffocate John Mateer and the Sooners under the new Jason Witten-led offense. Ole Miss has lived off of its offense for the past two seasons, and with how things have gone recently, a strong defensive showing in Norman will go a long way, not just towards a win but towards proving to the selection committee that the Rebels are worthy of making the postseason. Golding's defense has the talent to be great, now it just needs to translate to the field. Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images The Ole Miss Rebels take on the Oklahoma Sooners in Norman, Oklahoma. Kickoff is set for 4:15 p.m. EST on SEC Network. Ole Miss is favored by 1.5 points on the spread with a moneyline of -104. The total is set at 49.5 points. Here’s my Ole Miss vs. Oklahoma prediction and college football pick for Saturday, November 14, 2026. Ole Miss vs Oklahoma Prediction Ole Miss vs. Oklahoma Pick: Oklahoma -1 or Better My Oklahoma vs. Ole Miss best bet is on the Sooners. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page . Ole Miss vs Oklahoma Odds Ole Miss Odds 49.5 -110o / -110u Oklahoma Odds Ole Miss vs Oklahoma point spread : Ole Miss -1.5 (+110), Oklahoma +1.5 (-130) Ole Miss vs Oklahoma over/under : 49.5 (-110o / -110u) Ole Miss vs Oklahoma moneyline : Ole Miss -104, Oklahoma -115 Ole Miss vs Oklahoma College Football Preview I couldn't have been more wrong about last week's playoff rematch between Ole Miss and Georgia. The Rebels got absolutely stomped from start to finish in every facet. Now, with three losses under their belts and only games against Mississippi State and Wofford remaining over the final two weeks, I don't see a path to the College Football Playoff, which the Ole Miss locker room is likely fully aware of. There's a reason you're hearing about season-ending injuries and the portal already in Oxford. Do they show up this week in Norman? It's certainly a question worth posing for a team that had national title aspirations. Even if Ole Miss is fully locked in during practice all week and shows up ready to roll on Saturday, I still would feel confident holding a Sooners ticket. Let's start with injuries, where these two teams are headed in opposite directions. The Rebels recently learned star running back Kewan Lacy will shut it down for the remainder of the season. Plus, they will have to make do this week without their best offensive lineman in Patrick Kutas and leading tackler in linebacker Keaton Thomas. Meanwhile, the Oklahoma offensive line is finally getting back to full strength. The biggest addition was getting starting left tackle Michael Fasusi back a few weeks ago. There was previously a massive void at left tackle, which has since been filled by the former five-star who finally looked 100% healthy last week at Florida. Not only will pass protection improve immensely, but the running game should continue to look more competent the rest of the season, especially against an Ole Miss defense that has plenty of holes against the run and pass. Last week also marked the debut of Oklahoma's new play-caller, Jason Witten. I thought he did a fantastic job with play sequencing, and the entire operation just looked cleaner. Most importantly, Oklahoma didn't have any turnovers, which have absolutely killed them all season. Witten also unleashed John Mateer with a higher rate of designed runs. It also helps that Mateer is finally playing with confidence. Earlier in the season, he could barely scramble without literally dropping the ball and was extremely hesitant to fire on his reads. It was as if he almost had the quarterback version of the yips. With that said, it's not like this offense is going to turn into the 1999 Rams. This is still a team that's led by an elite defense that should get constant pressure on Trinidad Chambliss, especially without Kutas and a backfield that struggles in picking up blitzes. Chambliss has really struggled against the last two top-tier defenses he faced in Texas and Georgia. This is just not the same offense as last year. Not only is Lacy done for the year, but there's a new play-caller, and the pass-catchers aren't as talented. As a result, Chambliss' efficiency numbers have fallen precipitously when under pressure. That could spell doom against a Brent Venables stop unit that generates pressure at one of the highest rates in the country. From a regression standpoint, don't be surprised if Oklahoma falls on a key fumble or two. The Sooners have the lowest fumble recovery rate in the country at 23%, while the Rebels rank 20th in that department at nearly 80%. This is not my typical buy-low / sell-high spot, as Ole Miss got blown out last week, while Oklahoma pulled off a road upset. However, I still think this sets up well for the Sooners, who are trending up offensively with a defense that should give Chambliss fits. And I do question whether or not we get a fully locked-in Rebels bunch this week. picks.headline: 5 Ole Miss vs Oklahoma predictions with Trinidad Chambliss, Rebels' CFP chances on line
picks.blurb: 5 Ole Miss vs Oklahoma predictions with Trinidad Chambliss, Rebels' CFP chances on line - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Gane outlasts Hokit at UFC 334 College football winners/losers Texas ends LSU's playoff hopes Hicks tribute before BC-ND OU AD still peeved Sam Hutchens, Mississippi Clarion Ledger · The Clarion Ledger Thu, November 12, 2026 at 11:03 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads OXFORD − Ole Miss football must win on the road against Oklahoma to keep hopes of a College Football Playoff appearance alive. No. 17 Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) will play at Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3) on Nov. 14 (3:15 p.m., SEC Network). The Rebels are coming off a 42-7 home loss to No. 1 Georgia that put its CFP hopes on the edge of extinction. A viable path to the CFP begins with winning the final three games of the season. This is the third consecutive season Ole Miss has faced Oklahoma and the Rebels have won the first two matchups. Like Ole Miss, the Sooners made the College Football Playoff in 2025. OU returned quarterback John Mateer but has struggled to complement a strong defense with a steady offense. Although the Sooners have losses to Michigan, No. 1 Georgia, No. 13 Kentucky and No. 24 South Carolina, OU has beaten two teams that Ole Miss lost to in No. 8 Texas and Florida. Here are five predictions about the matchup, including the final score: Jason Witten will have new wrinkles for OU offense vs Ole Miss defense The matchup pits defensive coaches against each other in Ole Miss' Pete Golding and OU's Brent Venables. Interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten could be the wild card. The former Dallas Cowboys tight end was elevated to the interim offensive coordinator position after Oklahoma fired Ben Arbuckle. Five days after Arbuckle was dismissed, OU beat Florida 23-7 in a game where it had 351 total yards. The Oklahoma offense played clean, efficient football under Witten. The Sooners suddenly seem to have new life offensively, which comes at a bad time for an Ole Miss defense that was ravaged for 481 yards vs Georgia. Trinidad Chambliss, John Mateer both throw interceptions With three games remaining, Chambliss' interceptions have tripled this season. He threw three in a spectacular 2025 season, but is up to nine in 2026. Golding attributed the increase to a combination of bad reads, bad luck and bad throws. Chambliss has thrown at least one interception in seven games this season. That plays into the hands of Oklahoma, which is No. 4 in the SEC with nine interceptions. The Sooners are also No. 5 in the conference with 26 sacks. Chambliss has been more vulnerable when under pressure. OU quarterback John Mateer has had turnover problems as well. He's thrown seven interceptions and has two lost fumbles. Look for both defenses to come up with an interception. The Sooners' stingy defense is better prepared to recover from interceptions than Ole Miss. When OU picks off Chambliss, it will give the ball back to a Sooners' offense that looks well prepared to chew clock and limit the chances for the Rebels' offense. Ole Miss gives Makhi Frazier, Shekai Mills-Knight both at least 10 carries Even with a quarterback as capable as Chambliss, it will be hard for Ole Miss to attack Oklahoma through the air. OU has the No. 1 passing defense in the SEC (170.7 yards per game). OU is No. 7 in the SEC in rushing defense (122.6 yards per game), but it's the weaker of two stout options. Ole Miss needs running backs Shekai Mills-Knight and Makhi Frazier to play well. Those two players are the primary backs with Kewan Lacy ruled out with a shoulder injury. Mills-Knight and Frazier combined for 17 carries for 60 yards vs Georgia, but they should get more carries against Oklahoma. Oklahoma leads in time of possession, Ole Miss relies on big plays Opponents are 31-for-112 (27.7%) on third down conversions against the Sooners. That's the lowest mark in the SEC and No. 4 nationally. That indicates Ole Miss will have trouble maintaining long, slow-developing drives. The key to combat that is explosive plays. Ole Miss could use a big game from Deuce Alexander. The receiver leads Ole Miss with 669 receiving yards, but he was held without a catch against Georgia. He is Ole Miss' fastest, most explosive player and the primary threat to score a deep touchdown. Ole Miss is on the other end of the spectrum. The Rebels allow 44% of third down conversions, which is No. 14 in the SEC. The Sooners clinched the game against Florida with a 20-play march in the fourth quarter that consumed 12:45 on the clock. The Rebels must avoid that fate. Ole Miss vs Oklahoma score prediction Oklahoma 24, Ole Miss 23: This should be a close game that will be determined by whether Ole Miss' defense or Oklahoma's offense does better. Right now it feels like the OU offense has more momentum. The Rebels are more desperate, but feeling like you need to press and make big plays on the road against OU's defense is a bad place to be. Sam Hutchens covers Ole Miss for the Clarion Ledger.
