picks.blurb: Sooners Wire Staff predictions for Oklahoma vs. Ole Miss - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Gane outlasts Hokit at UFC 334 College football winners/losers Texas ends LSU's playoff hopes Hicks tribute before BC-ND OU AD still peeved Sooners Wire Staff predictions for Oklahoma vs. Ole Miss Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Oklahoma Sooners (5-4, 3-3 SEC) and the Ole Miss Rebels (6-3, 4-3 SEC ) meet for the third straight season and the second consecutive season in Norman. Oklahoma is 0-3 all-time in the series but is coming off of one of its most complete games of the season in their win over the Florida Gators . The offense found a rhythm and consistency we haven't seen much this year, and the defense suffocated the Florida Gators, holding them to seven points and forcing two interceptions. This week, with the Rebels coming to town, the Sooners face a much different challenge. Ole Miss boasts one of the most dynamic quarterbacks in college football, in Trinidad Chambliss. Chambliss is 15th in the nation in passing yards and second in the SEC behind LSU's Sam Leavitt. He's a threat to make plays with his legs as well, as we saw last year in the Rebels' win in Norman. On a slippery Owen Field, Chambliss threw for 315 yards and ran for 53 yards in Ole Miss's 34-26 win over Oklahoma. The Sooners defense will need to do a better job containing Chambliss if they want to win this Saturday and earn bowl eligibility. Can Oklahoma find a way to earn back-to-back victories for the first time since the LSU and Missouri wins at the end of last season? Here's how our staff at Sooners Wire sees the game playing out. Sooners Defense Leads to Win Oct 10, 2026; Dallas, Texas, USA; Oklahoma Sooners defensive back Peyton Bowen (22) runs to score a touchdown against the Texas Longhorns during the second half at Cotton Bowl. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images It'll be a battle between two defense-minded coaches, and the Sooners are still riding high with Interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten at the helm, while Ole Miss' offense is sputtering thanks to key injuries to its offensive line, star running back, and possibly the quarterback. For one of the few times this season, the injury report looks to be in favor of Oklahoma, which is looking to build on a win for the first time this season. With everyone theoretically healthy, one of the advantages Oklahoma has is that Ole Miss QB Trinidad Chambliss has become turnover-prone, throwing nine interceptions this season, while OU's defense does well at forcing those turnovers, coming in at No. 4 in the conference. It's no secret that the Sooners are typically successful when they win the turnover battle, and I think that will play a role in this one. It'll be a defensive battle, but OU will have the edge at home. Oklahoma 17, Ole Miss 14 James D. Jackson, Contributor Ole Miss Responds This season, Oklahoma has typically followed up an encouraging step forward with a discouraging step back, ever since the Texas game. Ole Miss is reeling after last week's loss to Georgia, and Brent Venables typically doesn't have his team as on point when the opponent is more desperate and hungry than the Sooners are. Things will probably slip after last week's upset win; there's too much of a pattern to think otherwise. If Trinidad Chambliss plays like he's capable of, Ole Miss wins. If OU recaptures some of the magic of last November, when the Sooners played consistent football, they can put an end to Ole Miss' teetering playoff hopes. Ole Miss 20, Oklahoma 17 Aaron Gelvin, Contributor Ole Miss has the Better QB Oct 31, 2026; Oxford, Mississippi, USA; Mississippi Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss (6) drops back to pass during the fourth quarter against the Auburn Tigers at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. The Sooners have yet to win or lose back-to-back games this season. While it looked much better offensively under Jason Witten, the question is whether that will continue against the Ole Miss Rebels. This game is a true toss-up, but I've got to go with the quarterback I trust more and that's Trinidad Chambliss. They found a way to win with a ball-control style that helped the Sooners win the time-of-possession battle by 15 minutes. The Sooners scored on three of their first four drives, laying the groundwork for what could be the plan to keep Trinidad Chambliss and the Rebels' offense at bay this weekend. Ole Miss allows 394.7 yards per game, which is 15th in the SEC and 104th in the nation. This could be another opportunity for the Sooners' offense to take a big step forward. away.blurb: No. 19 Ole Miss' side of the Student-Athlete Availability Report got cleaned up in Thursday night's update. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss and wide receiver Deuce Alexander were removed from the report. Both were listed as probable in the initial report Wednesday. Their availability for Saturday was never in much doubt. The same can't be said for the three Rebels listed as questionable, including one new addition. Running back Makhi Frazier was added to the report Thursday, joining defensive end Kam Franklin and safety Sharif Denson under the questionable designation. Frazier's addition is particularly concerning considering the Rebels are already without star running back Kewan Lacy, who has missed the last two games with a shoulder injury. Without Lacy, Frazier and Shekai Mills-Knight have been responsible for much of the workload in the Rebels' backfield. If Frazier can't play Saturday, Mills-Knight could be asked to take on an even larger role against the Sooners. Ole Miss is also dealing with significant injuries elsewhere on the roster. Starting right guard Patrick Kutas and linebacker Keaton Thomas are among the 11 Rebels ruled out for Saturday's game. Franklin and Denson, meanwhile, remain uncertain after appearing on both availability reports this week. The next update is scheduled for Friday night, with final designations coming before Saturday's kickoff in Norman. Ole Miss coach Pete Golding confirmed his squad will be without two of its most important offensive players when the Rebels line up against the Sooners. Golding said running back Kewan Lacy and starting offensive lineman Patrick Kutas will miss the game. So far this season, the Sooners have typically had the least desirable injury report. But the two losses for Ole Miss are fairly significant, especially given the Rebels are coming off their third loss of the season. Golding said Kutas was injured in Ole Miss’ 42-7 loss at Georgia on Nov. 7. The Rebels will have to make adjustments across the offensive line. Former Sooner Troy Everett will likely replace Kutas at right guard as he did against Georgia. “Not season-ending,” Golding said of Kutas’ injury in his weekly presser. “Kutas got banged up pretty good, so we will not have Patrick this week. So there will be some moving parts to that and looking at some guys bumping inside. Golding later clarified Lacy will not play either. Against the Sooners last season, Lacy rushed 27 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns to help No. 8 Ole Miss defeat No. 13 Oklahoma 34–26. This season, however, he has missed a handful of games due to injury. Lacy missed the Georgia game, and it was a noticeable absence. Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) mustered only 7 points against the Bulldogs. Lacy was a Doak Walker Award finalist last season. The honor is presented annually to the nation's top college football running back. He has run for five touchdowns this season but hasn’t seen the field since dislocating his shoulder against Texas in October. Ole Miss has lost two of the last three games in his absence. Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3 SEC) will have an opportunity to take advantage in Norman with kickoff scheduled for 3:15 p.m. CT. The game will be televised on the SEC Network. This is the third straight season the Sooners have played the Rebels and second straight season Oklahoma has hosted them. The league named the two schools annual rivals last season, meaning they'll play each other at home every season for at least the next four years. Ole Miss is 3-0 against the Sooners, who are trying to build on a 23-7 win over Florida . A win would also keep Oklahoma's bowl streak alive. home.headline: Tate Romney, Desmond Magiya Doubtful for Oklahoma State-Texas Tech Showdown
home.blurb: The Oklahoma State Cowboys have two important players listed as doubtful for Saturday’s game with the Texas Tech Red Raiders. Linebacker Tate Romney — who missed last week’s win over Kansas State due to injury — was listed as doubtful on the Cowboys’ first player availability report . Offensive lineman Desmond Magiya — who was not asked about during Tuesday’s press conference with head coach Eric Morris — was listed as doubtful. There is some good news for the Cowboys. Defensive end Jaleel Johnson , who missed last week’s game, was not listed on the player available report. Magiya is a valuable backup at multiple offensive line positions and is listed as left guard Johnny Dickson III’s backup at left guard. There was no indication during Saturday’s game against the Wildcats that Magiya suffered any sort of injury. His absence could impact the offensive line’s interior — if Dickson is unable to play. His status for the game is probable per the report. The Cowboys have listed three players as out for the game — wide receiver Dayvon Standard, tight end Carson Kolb and defensive tackle Landon Dean. Kolb is the only starter of the three. Without him, Oklahoma State has leaned on Oscar Hammond for the past two games. Texas Tech’s first report included four players listed as out, including wide receiver Coy Eakin, who has 22 catches this season and had one reception against West Virginia last weekend. Running back Cameron Dickey and linebacker Austin Romaine were both listed as questionable. Dickey played against WVU but only had three carries. Romaine, one of the top linebackers out of the transfer portal last season, had 15 tackles last week against the Mountaineers. Ole Miss coach Pete Golding confirmed his squad will be without two of its most important offensive players when the Rebels line up against the Sooners. Golding said running back Kewan Lacy and starting offensive lineman Patrick Kutas will miss the game. So far this season, the Sooners have typically had the least desirable injury report. But the two losses for Ole Miss are fairly significant, especially given the Rebels are coming off their third loss of the season. Golding said Kutas was injured in Ole Miss’ 42-7 loss at Georgia on Nov. 7. The Rebels will have to make adjustments across the offensive line. Former Sooner Troy Everett will likely replace Kutas at right guard as he did against Georgia. “Not season-ending,” Golding said of Kutas’ injury in his weekly presser. “Kutas got banged up pretty good, so we will not have Patrick this week. So there will be some moving parts to that and looking at some guys bumping inside. Golding later clarified Lacy will not play either. Against the Sooners last season, Lacy rushed 27 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns to help No. 8 Ole Miss defeat No. 13 Oklahoma 34–26. This season, however, he has missed a handful of games due to injury. Lacy missed the Georgia game, and it was a noticeable absence. Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) mustered only 7 points against the Bulldogs. Lacy was a Doak Walker Award finalist last season. The honor is presented annually to the nation's top college football running back. He has run for five touchdowns this season but hasn’t seen the field since dislocating his shoulder against Texas in October. Ole Miss has lost two of the last three games in his absence. Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3 SEC) will have an opportunity to take advantage in Norman with kickoff scheduled for 3:15 p.m. CT. The game will be televised on the SEC Network. This is the third straight season the Sooners have played the Rebels and second straight season Oklahoma has hosted them. The league named the two schools annual rivals last season, meaning they'll play each other at home every season for at least the next four years. Ole Miss is 3-0 against the Sooners, who are trying to build on a 23-7 win over Florida . A win would also keep Oklahoma's bowl streak alive. picks.headline: Kentucky vs Florida: Final thoughts, prediction
picks.blurb: Kentucky vs Florida: Final thoughts, prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Gane outlasts Hokit at UFC 334 College football winners/losers Texas ends LSU's playoff hopes Hicks tribute before BC-ND OU AD still peeved Story by Wildcats Wire Kentucky vs Florida: Final thoughts, prediction Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Fri, November 13, 2026 at 9:57 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Will Stein's Kentucky football team hosts Jon Sumrall's Florida Gators team under the lights at Kroger Field tomorrow at 6:15 P.M. ET. Florida has came back down to earth after a strong September and Kentucky is looking to bounce back after suffering their second loss of the season. We preview the Gators offense and defense, as well as laid out the path to victory for the Wildcats. Now, I will give my final thoughts on the matchup and a prediction for the game. Coach Stein said that last week was only the second time in his coaching career that his offense failed to score a touchdown. This team and the offense specifically will be looking to make a statement tomorrow night. They will get a perfect opportunity against a Brad White defense that has struggled all season for the Gators. As we know from watching years of Brad White's scheme in Lexington, they love to play soft zone coverage and allow easy completions to offenses in hopes of executing a bend-don't-break style of defense. The big advantage is this Kentucky offense is built off of efficiency and getting Kenny Minchey easy completions in quick game. This creates an advantageous scheme matchup for Will Stein and offensive coordinator Joe Sloan. If the Wildcats can eliminate the self-inflicted mistakes from last week in Knoxville, you have to like their chances to put together long scoring drives. The difference in this game being close and the Cats running away with it is if the offense can start to find the explosive plays. One area of this matchup we have not talked about is the weather aspect of this football game on Saturday. The past few days in Lexington have turned extremely cold, and temperatures for kickoff at looking at 40 degrees or below. Combine that with the winds, it will be freezing at Kroger Field and will only get colder as the game goes on. You have to wonder how this Florida team will respond in these conditions especially if they don't start fast in this one. This Florida team is reeling, they have lost four of their last five games. The drop-off has been eye-opening for the Gators because they looked like one of the best teams in the country through the first month of the season. Defenses have figured out how to bottle up their run game and the offense has started to suffer because of it. The Gators offense led them to their hot start to the Jon Sumrall era and covered up the rough play on the defensive side of the football. Kentucky has to stop this rushing attack and get Florida into a dropback heavy game. The Gators are going back to Aaron Philo after starting Tramell Jones last week. The old saying goes: if you have two quarterbacks, you have none. I think the Wildcats will be prepared to potentially see both guys this week as the Gators will try everything they can to generate some offense. Florida has to answer questions offensively, their offensive line is one of the worst in the conference and the quarterback situation is not ideal. Brad White has not figured out how to fix the Gators defensive issues in his first year away from Lexington. I think Kentucky capitalizes on that and has one of their best offensive performances of the season following last week where they failed to reach the end zone. Kentucky has their backs against the wall, they will make the College Football Playoff if they win the last three games and I believe the offense makes a statement in the cold at Kroger Field. Prediction: Kentucky 38, Florida 20 This article originally appeared on UK Wildcats Wire: Kentucky vs Florida: Final thoughts, prediction

picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Florida game glance, opening odds, and early prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Gane outlasts Hokit at UFC 334 College football winners/losers Texas ends LSU's playoff hopes Hicks tribute before BC-ND OU AD still peeved Kentucky vs. Florida game glance, opening odds, and early prediction dholbrook · SB Nation Mon, November 9, 2026 at 11:15 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Neither Kentucky nor Florida will feel good coming into this one. Kentucky dropped a stinker in Knoxville, losing 34-6, while Florida got whipped by Oklahoma in The Swamp, 23-7. But they'll both have to get over it quickly; the SEC comes at you fast. Florida will travel up to Kentucky for a November night game; the last time that happened was just last year. Kentucky rolled to a 38-7 victory. But both coaches are different, and I am not so sure a blowout is in the cards this year for either side. Both teams will look to right the ship and prevent one loss from becoming two. You better believe Jon Sumrall and Brad White will be coming back to Lexington with a win on their mind, while Kentucky will be looking to take the awful sting of that Volunteer loss out of their system while also keeping their College Football Playoff hopes afloat. Florida Gators (5-4, 3-4) Florida is a shockingly inconsistent team. The Gators destroyed Ole Miss by 24, knocked off Texas by 3, but lost by 28 to Missouri and 16 to Oklahoma. The Gators have been held to under 10 points in back-to-back games while also playing a QB carousel. Trammel Jones started against the Sooners but was a dreadful 10-of-22 with 2 INTs. But just a game before, Aaron Philo started 5-of-7, but those two incompletions were interceptions, and he was benched before halftime. Where the Gators go from there is anyone's guess, but Kentucky will need to prepare to see both guys. On defense, Florida is just as volatile. 425.3 total yards per game is what they give up for the year, but in the last 3 games, they have surrendered 278 yards to Texas, 318 to Georgia, and 351 to Oklahoma. So, Brad White has got his side playing a little better. But it really comes down to which team shows up. Will it be the team that knocked off Texas or the team that lost at home to Oklahoma? How to watch Kentucky Wildcats vs. Florida Gators Location: Kroger Field- Lexington, Kentucky Date: Saturday, November 14th Time: 6:15 PM ET Online streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening odds: FanDuel Sportsbook has Kentucky favored by 3.5 points with an over/under of 51.5. ESPN win probability: ESPN FPI gives Kentucky a 54% chance of victory Our prediction I'm not going to lie, this game has got weirdness written all over it. Kentucky and Florida are both coming off terrible losses, with both fan bases hurting. Whichever team handles that the best will walk away with a victory here. I think if Kentucky can get back to playing clean football, they have the talent and home-field advantage to send the Gators back home with a loss. But Florida has a lot of talent, and if they are motivated, they can beat anyone, anywhere, as proven down in Austin when they knocked off Texas. My biggest concern remains Malachi Wood, who has been abused by speed guys this season. Emmanuel Oyebadejo is a 6'6, 300-pound nightmare who leads the Gators with 4.5 sacks. You better believe he is licking his chops to go against the right side of Kentucky's line, which struggled down in Knoxville. Ultimately, I think Kentucky does clean it up, and despite some pressure off the edge, the Cats knock off the Gators. Former UK linebacker and assistant coach Jon Sumrall would be returning to Kroger Field as the Gators head coach. With Will Stein on the UK sideline, the game would feature a matchup of the two coaches viewed as the top candidates to replace Mark Stoops last season. But it would have been difficult to predict the greater stakes that would be on the line for Kentucky. Here is what you need to know about the matchup. What is at stake for Kentucky football vs. Florida Kentucky dropped from sixth to 11th in the playoff committee's top 25 after a loss at Tennessee. The good news for Stein and company is that ranking suggests Kentucky still controls its own destiny in the playoff race. If Kentucky wins its final three games, it should be in the field at 10-2. That quest starts with beating Florida on Saturday. Kentucky cannot be picky about wins, but the Wildcats could use some style points, too. Lopsided final scores in the losses to Alabama and Tennessee hurt the playoff resume, even if those games were close for most of three quarters. Winning comfortably in the remaining games would help alleviate concerns about the committee possibly jumping one-loss Texas Tech or one-loss Wake Forest ahead if they win out, too. The bigger threat might be from No. 18 USC, which also has two losses but still has resume-boosting opportunities against No. 9 Indiana and No. 4 UCLA remaining. Stein's team also remains in contention for a berth in the final SEC Championship Game, but it will need help. Kentucky needs to beat Florida and Missouri next week. away.blurb: Wide receiver Lawayne McCoy is expected to return after nearly a month on the sidelines, giving quarterback Lincoln Kienholz another important option in the passing game. Louisville WR LaWayne McCoy will return today after nearly a month, sources tell @On3. The coach also indicated that he did not expect McCoy to return immediately. However, the wide receiver’s recovery has progressed, and he was listed as probable on the ACC availability report ahead of Saturday’s matchup. McCoy’s return could be particularly important for Louisville’s offensive production. He has averaged 20.5 yards per reception across seven appearances this season. His 513 receiving yards and four touchdowns have made him one of the Cardinals’ most productive offensive weapons. Louisville’s offense is set to receive a timely boost as the Cardinals prepare for their road matchup against North Carolina. On3 national reporter Pete Nakos shared the development on X , reporting that McCoy will be back in action on Saturday. Nakos also highlighted McCoy’s production this season. writing: “(McCoy) Has 25 catches for 513 yards and 4 TDs this season. Cardinals are at North Carolina.” McCoy last played against Syracuse on October 17. He caught five passes for 93 yards in Louisville’s 34-26 victory. Further testing revealed that the injury was more serious than initially believed. The wide receiver subsequently missed Louisville’s games against Stanford and Georgia Tech. Louisville head coach Jeff Brohm initially provided a cautious update about McCoy’s recovery ahead of the Stanford game on Oct. 31. Speaking about the injury, Brohm said : “I don’t think it requires surgery, but we have to get it healed. So the timetable is kind of unknown now.” Louisville enters Saturday’s contest with considerable momentum. The Cardinals defeated Georgia Tech 44-17 on Nov. 7, extending their winning streak to four games. They currently hold a 6-3 overall record and a 5-2 mark in ACC play. away.headline: Billy Edwards Jr. suffers injury in UNC’s 16-14 loss to Louisville
away.blurb: Both defenses played way better than anybody expected for most of the night. Louisville did a great job of blitzing Billy Edwards Jr. and making him uncomfortable in the pocket, and ultimately it led to him ending up on the ground several times. The run game for the Heels wasn’t quite enough to do enough damage in the first half, and ultimately it led to them getting shut out of two quarters after Benjamin Hall was able to punch it in for the touchdown in the first quarter. On UNC’s final drive, Burgess was sacked for a two-yard loss, threw a couple of incompletions, and then threw a bizarre interception that effectively ended the game. The ball technically hit Jordan Shipp, but the ball went rogue and ended up in the hands of Jabari Mack. After Louisville killed the rest of the game clock, a skirmish broke out, but it’s unclear who started it. We’ll see what bad news the ACC delivers after the film is reviewed. Tonight’s game between UNC and Louisville was supposed to be closer to a shootout than a shutout, but ultimately both teams scored three touchdowns total in UNC’s frustrating 16-14 loss. As far as UNC’s defense goes, the mostly got pushed around on the line of scrimmage by Louisville’s run game, but they were able to get enough stops when it mattered most. After the Cardinals went up 13-7, the Heels clamped down and didn’t allow another touchdown for the rest of the night. Jaiden Patterson and Derek McDonald were key contributors in making sure the Cardinals didn’t have too much fun, racking up 17 tackles between the two. Where things took an unexpected turn is when Billy Edwards Jr. took a hard hit on a sack and had to leave the game. Freshman quarterback Travis Burgess took Edwards’ place, and his ability to punish defenses with his legs was on full display. It didn’t lead to any points until the fourth quarter, though, when he facilitated a nine-play, 75-yard drives that ended with Benjamin Hall finding the end zone once again. With a decent chunk of time left on the clock, the Heels’ defense was able to keep Louisville from adding more points to the board, and UNC regained possession with less than two minutes left in the game. UNC losing to Louisville isn’t really a surprise, but what is surprising is how they lost. They had a chance to win what was a lowish-scoring game in the fourth quarter, but not having Edwards in the game made things…different. Not good, not bad, just different. The Cardinals more than likely didn’t get to game plan for Burgess, but at the same time, it’s hard to imagine that Burgess expected to hear his name called after Edwards got hurt unless we’re all missing something. Bill Belichick tagging him in instead of Miles O’Neill feels like they knew Burgess was capable of escaping the kind of pressure Louisville kept throwing at Edwards, but we’ll see what is said during the post-game presser regarding how they decided to make that move. The Utes are ranked No. 2 in the latest CFP poll as one of two undefeated teams remaining. After beating their hated rivals BYU last week, Utah's path to the Playoff -- and the Big 12 title game -- is clear, but they must turn the page quickly from taking down the Cougars as a trip to Tucson could prove tricky. Arizona climbed to No. 23 in this week's rankings after beating TCU in a thriller, and the 7-2 Wildcats' only losses this season have been to the other top teams in the Big 12 -- BYU and Texas Tech . Both of those losses came on the road, and Arizona will be relishing the opportunity to prove they belong in the top tier of the Big 12 when they finally get to welcome one of the big boys to southern Arizona. For the Utes, a win writes their name into the CFP bracket in pencil, as they'd improve to 10-0 with two games left where they'd be heavy favorites over TCU and West Virginia . The Wildcats, meanwhile, can pick up the biggest win of Brent Brennan's tenure and solidify their place in the Big 12's upper tier. The game was originally scheduled for the 7:30 p.m. ET primetime slot on Saturday, but due to travel issues caused by the FAA shutdown on Friday , kickoff was moved to 10:30 p.m. for this pivotal showdown. Where to watch Utah vs. Arizona live Date : Saturday, Nov. 14 | Time : 10:30 p.m. ET Location : Casino Del Sol Stadium -- Tucson, Arizona TV: Fox | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Utah vs. Arizona: Need to know Refocusing the Utes: The Utes put everything they had into winning The Holy War last week against BYU, in the first-ever matchup between the rivals while both were ranked in the top 10. It was obvious how much they put into the game plan with their hot start, and then they were forced to dig deep and rally after the Cougars answered with some haymakers of their own. That win was a proof point for Morgan Scalley in his first season as head coach, but this week might show us more about the kind of culture he's building in Salt Lake City. There's a natural urge to exhale after that kind of win, but Arizona is going to be juiced up for the chance to face the No. 2 team in the country at home. The Utes have to find a way to match that energy -- or at least withstand an early onslaught -- and get the game back on their terms. Strength on strength in the pass game: Arizona is one of the best passing offenses in the country with veteran quarterback Noah Fifita who is both efficient with a 73% completion rate and dynamic with 23 pass plays of 30-plus yards -- third-most in the country. Fifita and his favorite target Isaiah Mizell can take the lid off of most defenses and apply constant stress -- especially with Fifita's ability to extend plays and get outside the pocket. However, they'll be going up against one of the nation's best pass defenses that had Bear Bachmeier completely lost a week ago. Utah is allowing opposing quarterbacks to complete just 51.3% of passes (2nd lowest in the country) and is tied for fourth in interceptions with 13 (including four last week). The Utes pass defense is hyper aggressive, and they have four players with two or more interceptions this season. If there is one weakness to the Utah defense, it is that they have been susceptible to big plays in the passing game. The Utes have allowed 15 pass plays of 30+ yards this season, which ranks 104th in the country. Fifita and Arizona will have to take advantage of those opportunities for chunk plays when they present themselves because moving the ball consistently against the Utes is incredibly difficult. Arizona's pass rush vs. Devon Dampier : The Utes defense will get plenty of attention, but Arizona hasn't been a slouch on that side of the ball this year either. The strength of their defense is their pass rush, which is 10th in the nation in sacks per game (3.11). Devon Dampier is a tough quarterback to wrangle with his combination of strength and elusiveness, but the Wildcats are going to try to heat up Dampier to create some negative plays or, more ideally, turnovers. How Utah's offensive line handles Arizona's rush and how Dampier manages plays when the Wildcats do get pressure on him will be critical in this game. Utah has allowed just 13 sacks this season, thanks to a quality offensive line and Dampier's escapability, but that will be put to the test against the Wildcats. If Arizona is going to win this game, they need to find ways to get the Utes' offense behind the sticks and probably need to win the turnover battle. The pass rush is going to be their best weapon to accomplish both of those goals, and if Arizona is going to pull off the upset, expect the pass rush to be leading the charge. Utah vs. Arizona prediction, picks The Wildcats are a good football team and should provide a big test for the Utes coming off last week's win. That said, so far this season, when Arizona has played the best teams in the Big 12, it has proven to be lagging just a bit behind. Over 60 minutes, I expect that to be the case again on Saturday, even with a raucous environment in Tucson for their biggest home game in years. Utah won't have it easy, but when the clock hits triple zeroes, I expect the Utes to move to 10-0 and cover the short number. (Photo by Chris Gardner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brian Pedersen · SB Nation Tue, November 10, 2026 at 8:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads During their decade-plus together in the Pac-12, Arizona and Utah had plenty of great battles, but the results tended to be streaky. The Wildcats won four straight meetings from 2012-15, then Utah took six in a row before the UA claimed the last two, including their Big 12 debut in 2024 when it beat a Top 10 Utes squad on the road. But the opponent coming to Tucson this weekend is better than any of those previous versions. Utah is 9-0 and ranked No. 2 nationally, one of two unbeaten teams in FBS. To better understand the Utes, we reached out to Josh Furlong of KSL.com for some insight and a score prediction. Below are his spirited answers to our lifeless questions: AZ Desert Swarm: What have been the main keys to Utah getting off to its best start since 2008? Josh Furlong: "The easy answer is quarterback Devon Dampier, who has been healthy and efficient as the team's biggest playmaker, but it ultimately comes down to the culture Morgan Scalley has built at Utah in such a short time. He's allowing the players to be loose while focused, understanding that it takes each person to contribute to wins. He's an extremely competitive coach, but he's able to pair that with a system that allows players to make mistakes, grow and develop." Arizona fans still have nightmares about Devon Dampier from two years ago at New Mexico, and he seems to have only gotten better. Where has his game most improved this season, and is there anything he still struggles with? "Dampier has worked on going through his progressions and staying in the pocket more, which has allowed Utah to do more with him at QB. It's giving him more structure while understanding that he still needs room to freelance and be the dynamic QB he can be. All of that has allowed him to have more confidence, especially now that he's been paired with a better group of wide receivers. At times, though, he gets happy feet and doesn't have the right mechanics in his throws, which can sometimes limit his passing." Wayshawn Parker apparently got banged up against BYU but should be good to go for this game. What does he bring to the offense when healthy? "Wayshawn Parker simply opens up the options for Utah's offense. His threat as a runner, especially as he breaks through tackles, makes him one of the top offensive names you have to take away. But by doing so, opposing defenses have to handle many other players that can be just as effective in advancing the offense — Dampier, Daniel Bray, Byrd Ficklin, Braden Pegan, Creed Whittemore, etc. On top of that, he's really developed a great pass blocking game, which has been a huge advantage in keeping Dampier upright and doing what he does." Arizona's secondary has been dealing with injuries and got exploited a bit last week with deep passes. Who would be the beneficiaries of this in the Ute receiving corps? "The primary receiving target would be Braden Pegan (WR1), who is a multi-faceted receiver who can do pretty much anything needed, and is paired with Ricky Johnson and Creed Whittemore. Johnson is a smooth runner with great separation and great hands. Whittemore works primarily in the slot and has been great in the intermediate game, especially with opposing defenses focusing on Pegan and the potential run threats of Dampier, Ficklin, Parker. Another option is tight end Noah Bennee, who is the benefactor of all the other skills players being the top of mind. As the defense focuses on other players, Bennee sneaks out and can be a problem with his size." How do you expect Utah to defend Arizona's passing attack? "Utah will primarily operate in man coverage and force Noah Fifita to beat them one-on-one, while the defensive coordinator Colton Swan schemes up disguises and blitzes to keep Fifita uncomfortable. Because Fifita is so explosive, it's likely Utah will try more contain while pressuring him." Morgan Scalley had been the coach in waiting at Utah for a while, and we're seeing why with this 9-0 start. What are the biggest differences between him and Kyle Whittingham? "The biggest difference is that Scalley is a people's person. Kyle Whittingham cared more about coaching football and not the other elements, whereas Scalley sees it all interconnected. He shares the same hard-nosed, physical approach of Whittingham but wants a connected team that has no factions. It's not, offense gets to know offense and defense gets to know defense, it's a team-wide look as each works to understand the other. He's also open to feedback, assuming that the feedback actually is presented in a way that helps change and it's just complaining, though he'd listen to anyone who is frustrated. He wants all to feel connected and bought into the program, regardless of their standing with the team." Prediction time. Does Utah move one step closer to an unbeaten regular season or does Arizona pull off a November upset at home and stay in the hunt for the Big 12 title game and the playoffs? Give us a score pick. "This game in Tucson is always a tricky one. Even when Utah has been the clear favorite, it's far from a decisive win for the Utes. I think Scalley has his squad more focused on this game than it might have been in year's past, which leads me to believe Utah will be ready for any blow and not be caught off guard in a road environment. I think Utah is the more complete team, but they've got to stop Fifita. To me, Utah wins this game if they can contain Fifita (as much as possible) and cannot give up momentum to an opposing crowd. I see Utah winning something like 31-24 ."

They were 0-for-4 on fourth down (against Alabama last week), and they were abysmal in the red zone. But I think you can fix those things, so I'm leaning toward LSU making the adjustments that they need to and winning the football game." Some fans might have expected Kelly to pick Texas for a few reasons. For starters, the Longhorns have a better collection of wins and are on a three-game winning streak. picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for Texas' Saturday Night Showdown Against LSU Skip to main content SI.COM LONGHORNS NEWS 2025 Football Bracket FOOTBALL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2023 FOOTBALL COMMITS SI.COM LONGHORNS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM LONGHORNS BB The trouble with bold predictions is they tend to sound a little ridiculous — right up until they happen. There are plenty of reasonable expectations for Saturday night’s matchup between Texas and LSU. But reasonable expectations aren’t all that interesting, are they? So let’s throw a little caution to the wind. Maybe these predictions will look brilliant by the final whistle. Maybe they’ll be aging poorly before halftime. But that’s half the fun in the first place. Here are three bold predictions for the Longhorns’ trip to Baton Rouge. Raleek Brown Rushes for Over 100 Yards Nov 7, 2026; Columbia, Missouri, USA; Texas Longhorns running back Raleek Brown runs the ball during the first half against the Missouri Tigers at Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium. William Purnell-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect On paper, this might be the boldest prediction of the three. On paper, this might be the boldest prediction of the three. LSU enters Saturday allowing just 84.7 rushing yards per game, the second-best mark in the SEC. Meanwhile Texas has struggled to establish consistency on the ground for much of the season. But if there’s a Longhorn capable of bucking that trend, it’s Raleek Brown. Against Ole Miss, Brown demonstrated what an elite Texas run game could look like given the opportunity, carrying the ball 23 times for 157 yards. Last weekend, he once again flashed that potential, rushing for 85 yards on 17 attempts. With Sarkisian emphasizing the importance of avoiding situations where Texas falls behind the chains, establishing the run game early will likely be a priority. That could mean a concerted effort to feed Brown from the opening drive, allowing him to find his rhythm. It certainly won't be easy against an LSU defensive front that has made life miserable for opposing running backs all season. But if Sarkisian can get Brown going, don't be surprised if he eclipses the century mark. Colin Simmons Records Three Sacks Oct 10, 2026; Dallas, Texas, USA; Texas Longhorns defensive end Colin Simmons in action during the game against the Oklahoma Sooners at the Cotton Bowl. Before his ankle injury, it would’ve been fair to argue that Colin Simmons was the best defensive player in the nation. Through his first six games, the junior accumulated 10.5 sacks — a metric he still leads the SEC in despite missing more than 2 games — and 16 tackles for loss. After playing just 18 snaps against Missouri, Simmons has yet to fully establish himself as the disruptive force that terrorized opposing offenses earlier in the season. Saturday might change that. LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt was sacked four times against Alabama last weekend, and Texas’ defensive front will prove to be another difficult assignment. But perhaps the most intriguing aspect of this prediction is Leavitt’s style of play. Leavitt has demonstrated a willingness to escape the pocket and improvise when plays begin to break down, often extending plays with his legs in hopes of creating something out of nothing. And while that ability makes him a dangerous dual-threat quarterback, it could also present an opportunity for a player with Simmons’ speed and relentless pursuit. Simmons doesn't necessarily need to beat his blocker immediately to disrupt a play. His closing speed allows him to pursue quarterbacks well after they've escaped the initial pressure, potentially turning Leavitt's improvisation into opportunities for sacks. Yes, three sacks is asking a lot, especially from a player still working his way back from an ankle injury. But if Simmons is even close to full strength, there's little reason to believe he can't once again take over a game. Texas Forces Three Turnovers Nov 7, 2026; Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA; LSU Tigers quarterback Sam Leavitt looks to pass the ball during the second half against Alabama Crimson Tide at Tiger Stadium. Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Nine interceptions in nine games. Nine interceptions in nine games. That’s the rather alarming statistic surrounding Leavitt , even if those numbers don’t necessarily tell the full story. Not all nine interceptions have been his fault. But Leavitt has shown a tendency to misread defenders dropping into coverage and force throws into crowded windows, mistakes that Texas could be well-positioned to exploit. The Tigers have committed 13 turnovers this season, including four lost fumbles. And while Texas has forced just 10 turnovers through nine games, with Simmons healthy, Rasheem Biles playing some of his best football and a secondary capable of capitalizing on hurried throws, the Longhorns have all the pieces to give Texcalibur quite the night.
